q: We buy diesel in jerry cans for forklifts and small engines. How do we record it for carbon?
title: Diesel bought in jerry cans
short: Count it like any other diesel: litres bought times 2.68 kg CO2 per litre, in Scope 1. Keep the pump bill for each fill, or a cash memo with litres, date and amount. A simple can issue log shows which machine used it if a buyer asks.
audience: Workshops and factories with forklifts, pumps and small generators

ul: Pump bill or memo with litres for each fill.
A log: date, can, litres, machine.
Cans still full at year end, if you count consumption rather than purchases.

p: Diesel at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre, from IPCC 2006 defaults. It is Scope 1 because you burn it in your own equipment.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site, and labels estimates as estimates.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative)
lines: 15 fills of a 20 litre can = 300 litres
